fields.meta_title: Holiday Landing Page Builder for Seasonal Sales | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a holiday landing page from a prompt. See a gift finder, shipping cutoffs, Christmas Eve RSVPs, and office gift orders. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Holiday Landing Page That Works the Whole Season
fields.hero_description: Build a holiday landing page from one prompt, with each gift request and RSVP saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for a Holiday Campaign
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the holiday landing page from your prompt, plus the table that keeps each gift request and RSVP.
fields.feature_1:
Your seasonal offer, written into a page

Describe the holiday, the offer, and the last day it runs. Emergent builds the page around that one offer, with a section for gifts and one for dates. Prompt again to change it.
fields.feature_2:
A gift finder shoppers can narrow

Ask for the recipient and a price range. The app shows only the items that match both answers, and a shopper can save the picks to a list along with an email address for later.
fields.feature_3:
Dates that change what the page shows

Set the last day for each shipping option or signup. When that date passes, the app closes the option and moves the next open one to the top, with its order-by date beside it.
fields.feature_4:
Every request in a database you own

The app saves each gift list, order request, and RSVP to a database you own. Each row keeps the answers and the date it came in, and the table sorts by any column next year.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when an order request arrives

Pick email, Slack, or an in-app alert for new requests. The app sends one with the details as each request comes in, and a reminder follows if nobody replies by the next morning.
fields.feature_6:
Publish on your domain, keep the code

Put the page on your own domain, such as shop.yourstore.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Six candles for a host, under $40

Shoppers at Kestwick Candle Co. pick who the gift is for and a budget, and the page shows only the candles that fit. A host under $40 brings up 6 candles. In the first week of December 418 shoppers used the finder and 157 saved a gift list with their email, Seraphine Margolin among them.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each shipping option closes by its own date

Harbrook Pottery posts a date beside every shipping option: standard orders by Dec 16, express by Dec 20. On each date the page closes that option and moves the next one to the top. On Dec 17 shoppers see standard marked closed and express first. After Dec 20 the page offers studio pickup through Dec 23.
fields.tab_content_3:
When 4:00 pm fills, families see 6:00 pm

Larkspur Hill Chapel lists 3 Christmas Eve services with 220 seats each, the last at 11:00 pm. Families RSVP with their party size, and the page counts down the seats left. A full service points to the next time with room. By Dec 18 the 4:00 pm service was full and the 6:00 pm had 37 seats left.
fields.tab_content_4:
A $672 request from 24 Classic boxes

An office manager tells Ovenbird Bakery's page how many people are on the gift list and picks a box size. The page multiplies the two and emails the request to the bakery. Nomvula Mkhize at Pellworth Dental asked for 24 Classic boxes at $28 each: a $672 request, saved with her Dec 19 delivery date.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Holiday Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to plan a holiday landing page around one offer and its dates, then build and publish it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one holiday and one offer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set every date before you write
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the offer in one line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the offer needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the holiday the page is for and the single offer it carries, such as office gift boxes for Christmas or a pie order for Thanksgiving. A page that tries to sell everything in the store at once leaves shoppers choosing instead of buying.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the dates that change the page: the day the offer opens, each order-by date, and the final day of the offer. Check your carrier's published holiday schedule before you promise a shipping date, and leave a day of margin.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the offer as one line a shopper could repeat to a friend, like free gift wrap on every order through Dec 22. Put it at the top of the page with its end date right under it, where nobody has to scroll.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what the page asks each visitor. A gift finder needs a recipient and a budget; an RSVP needs a party size; an office order needs a headcount. Every extra field is one more reason to leave before the form is sent.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the plan into Emergent with the offer, the dates, and the questions in plain words. Emergent builds a page with its own table, and you prompt again to move a date or rewrite any section before launch.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan what shows after the season
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide now what the page shows once the last date passes: a thank-you note, a signup for next year's list, or a link back to the store. A holiday page left as it was in January points people at an offer that has ended.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place a test order or RSVP and check that the row lands in your table and the email alert arrives. Then publish on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits, and share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a holiday landing page?
faq_plan.a: A holiday landing page is a standalone web page built for one seasonal campaign, such as a Christmas gift guide or a church's Christmas Eve services. It carries a single offer with its own dates, and it changes or comes down once the season is over.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a holiday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write down the holiday, the offer, and every date that changes the page, then describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. You get the page and a database for every request, and a new prompt moves a date or rewrites a section before you publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a Christmas landing page include?
faq_plan.a: A Christmas landing page needs one offer, the date it ends, and one action for the visitor, such as an order, an RSVP, or a saved gift list. A store page adds the last day to order for delivery before Christmas. A church page also lists its service times and how families RSVP.

faq_plan.q: Can one holiday landing page cover every sale of the season?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the offers share the same dates and rules; split them when they do not. A doorbuster with a countdown belongs on a black friday landing page, while a gift finder or a set of shipping cutoffs can run on one holiday page from November to late December.

faq_plan.q: When should a holiday landing page go live?
faq_plan.a: Put it live before the first email or ad that links to it, with time to test every date rule. Pick the day from your own calendar: the first day the offer is valid, with a test order placed the day before. Emergent changes the page by prompting: moving a date takes one new prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I show shipping deadlines on a holiday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put an order-by date beside each shipping option, near the top of the page and again by the order button. Take the dates from your carrier's own holiday schedule, add a day of margin, and set the page to close each option when its date passes.

faq_plan.q: How do I see which promotion sent visitors to my holiday landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give each promotion its own link with a tag, such as ?src=newsletter, and save that tag with every order request or signup. If creators share the offer, an influencer landing page for each creator keeps their visitors and signups apart from the rest.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with a holiday landing page after the season ends?
faq_plan.a: Keep it and change it. Leave the page at the same address and replace the offer with whatever comes next; old links in emails and posts then still land somewhere. This year's requests stay in your own database, ready when you plan next year's version.

faq_plan.q: How many offers should one holiday landing page show?
faq_plan.a: One, or two at most. A single offer with one action and one end date is easier to read and to test than a page listing every deal in the store. Put any second offer lower on the page, with its own date beside it.

faq_plan.q: Can a holiday landing page sign up volunteers for a toy drive?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for a name, an email, and the shift each volunteer wants, and close a shift once it fills. A charity that runs drives all year may want a nonprofit landing page that stays up, with the holiday drive as one section. Emergent builds the shift list and the signup table from one prompt.
